title: On-call Accountability Guide and Escalation Scenarios
author: Priya Kapoor
content:
Summary:
This document defines who is accountable during incidents, concrete escalation scenarios, triage and remediation checklists, on-call rotation guidance, and reproducible game day exercises. It is intended for engineers, SREs, and on-call responders who will execute runbooks and communicate with internal and external stakeholders.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood-hosted services (api.redwood.internal, inference-gw, router, kv-cache).
- Covers severity classification, primary/secondary responsibilities, escalation paths, status page updates, and post-incident follow-up.
- Does not replace service-specific runbooks (links in Related pages).

Principles (short):
- Act with ownership: responders should act until a handoff is explicit.
- Fast, clear communication: update channels every 15 minutes for Sev0/Sev1 until recovery.
- Avoid cognitive overload: prefer escalation to an IC when scope grows beyond one responder.

Incident lifecycle (high level):
1) Detection & Alerting: PagerDuty alerts + automated monitoring (CloudWatch/Prometheus).
2) Triage (first 10 minutes): confirm scope, impact, and assign primary responder.
3) Containment (15–60 minutes): mitigate customer impact (fallbacks, routing, scale-up).
4) Remediation (hours): deploy fixes, rollbacks, or configuration changes.
5) Recovery confirmation: validate SLOs and monitor for regressions.
6) Post-incident: blameless postmortem, RCA, and action items.

Roles & responsibilities:
- Primary Responder (PR): first engineer to acknowledge alert. Responsibilities: collect logs, run triage checklist, apply short-term mitigations, own incident channel.
- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates multi-team activity for Sev0/Sev1. Responsibilities: communication cadence, prioritization, deciding customer comms, engagement of execs if needed.
- SRE Owner: owns platform-level remediations (autoscaling, capacity, network).
- Service Lead / Oncall SME: subject-matter expert for the affected service.
- Communications Lead: drafts external status updates and customer notifications.
- Postmortem Author: writes the formal incident report.

Severity definitions and thresholds:
- Sev0 (P0) — System-wide critical outage: >50% of requests failing or >90% latency regression across regions for >5 minutes. Action: immediate IC, executive notification.
- Sev1 (P1) — Customer-impacting outage: significant subset of customers degraded (>10%). Action: IC if escalation needed; hourly exec updates after 1 hour.
- Sev2 (P2) — Partial degradation: single region or non-critical functionality affected. Action: PR-led containment, oncall SME engaged.
- Sev3 (P3) — Minor impact: edge errors, limited customers, or operational tasks. Action: ticketation and fix during normal hours.

Escalation matrix (text table):
| Trigger / Time | Primary responder action | If unresolved after | Escalate to | Channel |
|----------------|-------------------------|---------------------|-------------|---------|
| PagerDuty alert acknowledged | Run triage checklist | 10 minutes | Service Lead | #svc-<name>-incidents |
| Impact confirmed (Sev1/Sev0) | Call an IC and create incident channel | 15 minutes | Incident Commander | #incidents |
| No progress on mitigation | Notify SRE Owner, request capacity increase/fallback | 30 minutes | Platform Oncall | #sre-oncall |
| Exec notification required | IC to inform Head of Eng & CEO | 60 minutes (Sev0) | Exec on-call | direct pager/email |

Triage checklist (first 10 minutes):
- Confirm what is failing (API endpoints, model quality, embeddings, telemetry).
- Confirm blast radius (regions, accounts, routes).
- Check recent deploys/rollouts (Console rollouts page).
- Capture logs and span traces: link to the tracing session and relevant logs.
- Verify capacity signals: GPU utilization, queue depth, OOMs.
- Apply immediate mitigations: route to fallback model, scale replicas, enable read-only mode.
- Create incident channel and update PagerDuty incident with notes and links.

Runbook starter (generic, can be copy-pasted into service runbooks):
1) Validate alert: `kubectl get pods -n <ns>`; `kubectl logs -f <pod>`; `curl -sv https://api.redwood.internal/health`
2) Check autoscaling: `kubectl describe hpa <svc>` or `cloudctl describe autoscaler <svc>`
3) Check GPU health: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,memory.used --format=csv` (on-host) or open telemetry panels.
4) Roll back recent deploy: follow CI/CD rollback docs; prefer config toggles if possible.
5) Apply circuit-breaker: update router config to reduce new sessions to degraded path.
6) If kernel OOMs: capture core and escalate to infra kernel team.

Example escalation scenarios (concrete):
Scenario A — Inference gateway returning 500s across region after a config rollout:
- Triage: PR checks recent rollout id (Console) -> matches 12:05 deploy.
- Action: Immediately rollback to prior revision (CI/CD rollback step).
- Escalation: If rollback fails in 15 minutes, IC calls SRE Owner to route traffic to standby region and open cloud provider ticket.
- Customer comms: initial status set to "investigating" within 20 minutes, follow-up every 30 minutes until recovery.

Scenario B — Model quality regression (higher hallucinations) observed by automated evals:
- Triage: Confirm eval set regressions and ratio of affected requests.
- Action: Pin customers to verified model version; disable auto-routing to the new model.
- Escalation: Notify ML model onboarding and product leads if >5% error rate.
- Customer comms: targeted notification to affected customers via email template (see example).

Scenario C — Network partition between control plane and VPC-hosted private deployment:
- Triage: Confirm routes and BGP sessions, check VPC flow logs.
- Action: Failover to Private control plane snapshot or instruct customer to use local endpoints per private deployment runbook.
- Escalation: Engage Private deployments oncall and account owner.

Communication cadence and templates:
- Internal updates (Sev0/Sev1): every 15 minutes until containment; every 30 minutes during remediation.
- External status page cadence: initial update within 20 minutes, follow-ups at 40 minutes, 2 hours, 6 hours, and when resolved.

Status page & customer message templates (placeholders):
- Initial short update (public status page):
  Subject: Incident — API request failures affecting <region>
  Body: "We are investigating increased error rates for the Redwood API impacting <region>. Our engineers are actively triaging. We will provide an update by <time>. Impact: some requests may fail with 500 errors."

- Targeted customer email (example):
  Subject: Service interruption affecting your Redwood inference requests
  Body: "Hi <CustomerName>, we’re investigating an issue impacting inference requests in <region>. We’ve rolled back a deployment and are monitoring recovery. No customer data exposure has been detected. We’ll follow up within 60 minutes. If you have immediate concerns, reply or open a ticket at <support link>."

- Post-resolution update:
  Body: "The issue has been resolved by <action taken>. We are completing a post-incident review; a preliminary RCA will be published within 72 hours. We apologize for the impact."

Escalation call templates (IC -> Exec):
- Short briefing format (5 lines):
  1) What happened (time, services affected).
  2) Current impact (customers, % requests failing, business exposure).
  3) What we’ve done (mitigations applied).
  4) Next steps and ETA.
  5) Decision needed from execs (if any).

On-call rotation and handoff guidance:
- Shifts: weekly rotations for SREs and service oncalls (Mon 9am local).
- Handoff notes: outgoing oncall must post a handoff message with known issues, active incidents, and monitoring dashboards. Use the template in the team wiki.
- Handoff checklist:
  - Confirm PagerDuty schedule membership.
  - Confirm Slack notification routing.
  - Verify telemetry dashboards are accessible.
  - List ongoing work that may affect availability (ongoing rollouts, infra changes).

Game day exercise playbook (reproducible):
- Objective: validate the incident lifecycle, communication cadence, and runbook efficacy; measure time-to-detect and time-to-recover.
- Frequency: quarterly for SRE, semi-annual per service owner.
- Roles: designate a facilitator, observers (measurements), responders (rotate).
- Example exercises:
  1) Simulated config rollout causing 50% error rate — test rollback and cross-region failover.
     - Success criteria: rollback completed <15 minutes, public status updated in <20 minutes.
  2) Artificial model-quality regression — test model pinning and customer notifications.
     - Success criteria: affected customers identified and pinned within 30 minutes.
  3) Control plane latency spike — test alerting thresholds and IC activation.
     - Success criteria: IC created and incident channel opened within 10 minutes.
- Post-game-day: produce a short report with timings, gaps, and action items.

Post-incident process and timelines:
- Incident triage note posted to incident channel within 1 hour.
- Preliminary RCA summary published within 72 hours (draft by IC + responders).
- Full postmortem (blameless) published within 7 days with owners for each action item and deadlines.
- Action items tracked in the engineering backlog and reviewed in the next team retro.

Operational metrics to track per incident:
- Time to acknowledge (target <5 min).
- Time to containment (target P0 <30 min, P1 <60 min).
- Time to recovery (target P0 <2 hours).
- Number of pages per incident.
- Communication latency (time between incident detection and first public update).

Ownership and continuous improvement:
- ICs and PRs should nominate at least one deep action item for each Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- The SRE management team consolidates recurring action items into quarterly reliability initiatives.

Related pages (examples):
- /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks/api-gateway-recovery
- /confluence/eng-platform/incident-command-cheat-sheet
- /confluence/eng-infra/capacity-scaling-guidelines

Appendix: quick CLI snippets and runbook links
- Rollback (CI): `ci rollback --service inference-gw --to-revision <rev>`
- Create incident channel: `/incident create \"<short title>\" --severity P1` (Slack bot)
- PagerDuty escalation: `pd incidents acknowledge <id>`
- Example logs query (ELK): `timestamp:[now-15m TO now] AND status:500 AND service:inference-gw`

Document maintenance:
- Owner: eng-sre (policy owner); please review annually or after any Sev0/Sev1 incident.
- For edits: submit a PR to the Confluence doc with reviewers listed above.
